1 │ HTTPie: cURL for humans
   2 │ =======================
   3 │ 
   4 │ **HTTPie is a CLI HTTP utility** built out of frustration with existing tools. The goal is to make CLI interaction with HTTP-based services as human-friendly as possible.
   5 │ 
   6 │ HTTPie does so by providing an ``http`` command that allows for issuing arbitrary HTTP requests using a **simple and natural syntax** and displaying **colorized responses**:
   7 │ 
   8 │ .. image:: https://github.com/jkbr/httpie/raw/master/httpie.png
   9 │     :alt: HTTPie compared to cURL
  10 │ 
  11 │ Under the hood, HTTPie uses the excellent `Requests <http://python-requests.org>`_ and `Pygments <http://pygments.org/>`_ Python libraries. Python 2.6+ is supported (including 3.x).
  12 │ 
  13 │ Installation
  14 │ ------------
  15 │ 
  16 │ The latest **stable version** of HTTPie can always be installed (or updated to) via `pip <http://www.pip-installer.org/en/latest/index.html>`_::
  17 │ 
  18 │     pip install -U httpie
  19 │ 
  20 │ 
  21 │ Or, you can install the **development version** directly from GitHub:
  22 │ 
  23 │ .. image:: https://secure.travis-ci.org/jkbr/httpie.png
  24 │     :target: http://travis-ci.org/jkbr/httpie
  25 │     :alt: Build Status of the master branch
  26 │ 
  27 │ ::
  28 │ 
  29 │     pip install -U https://github.com/jkbr/httpie/tarball/master
  30 │ 
  31 │ 
  32 │ Usage
  33 │ -----
  34 │ 
  35 │ Hello world::
  36 │ 
  37 │     http GET httpie.org
  38 │ 
  39 │ Synopsis::
  40 │ 
  41 │     http [flags] METHOD URL [items]
  42 │ 
  43 │ There are four types of key-value pair items available:
  44 │ 
  45 │ Headers (``Name:Value``)
  46 │    Arbitrary HTTP headers. The ``:`` character is used to separate a header's name from its value, e.g., ``X-API-Token:123``.
  47 │ 
  48 │ Simple data fields (``field=value``)
  49 │   Data items are included in the request body. Depending on the ``Content-Type``, they are automatically serialized as a JSON ``Object`` (default) or ``application/x-www-form-urlencoded`` (the ``-f`` flag). Data items use ``=`` as the separator, e.g., ``hello=world``.
  50 │ 
  51 │ Raw JSON fields (``field:=value``)
  52 │   This item type is needed when ``Content-Type`` is JSON and a field's value is a ``Boolean``, ``Number``,  nested ``Object`` or an ``Array``, because simple data items are always serialized as ``String``. E.g. ``pies:=[1,2,3]``.
  53 │ 
  54 │ File fields (``field@/path/to/file``)
  55 │   Only available with ``-f`` / ``--form``. Use ``@`` as the separator, e.g., ``screenshot@/path/to/file.png``. The presence of a file field results into a ``multipart/form-data`` request.
  56 │ 
  57 │ 
  58 │ Examples
  59 │ ^^^^^^^^
  60 │ ::
  61 │ 
  62 │     http PATCH api.example.com/person/1 X-API-Token:123 name=John email=john@example.org age:=29
  63 │ 
  64 │ 
  65 │ The following request is issued::
  66 │ 
  67 │     PATCH /person/1 HTTP/1.1
  68 │     User-Agent: HTTPie/0.1
  69 │     X-API-Token: 123
  70 │     Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
  71 │ 
  72 │     {"name": "John", "email": "john@example.org", "age": 29}
  73 │ 
  74 │ 
  75 │ It can easily be changed to a 'form' request using the ``-f`` (or ``--form``) flag, which produces::
  76 │ 
  77 │     PATCH /person/1 HTTP/1.1
  78 │     User-Agent: HTTPie/0.1
  79 │     X-API-Token: 123
  80 │     Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=utf-8
  81 │ 
  82 │     age=29&name=John&email=john%40example.org
  83 │ 
  84 │ It is also possible to send ``multipart/form-data`` requests, i.e., to simulate a file upload form submission. It is done using the ``--form`` / ``-f`` flag and passing one or more file fields::

  86 │     http -f POST example.com/jobs name=John cv@~/Documents/cv.pdf

  92 │         <input type="file" name="cv" />
  93 │     </form>
